config.title: Write an anagram checker

intro.title: Write an anagram checker
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a simple anagram checker—a program that determines if two given words are anagrams of each other. An anagram is a word formed by rearranging the letters of another word, using all the original letters exactly once. You will learn to compare strings by manipulating and sorting their characters, using core JavaScript concepts like string methods, arrays, and conditional logic. This hands-on exercise will help you practice fundamental programming skills in a clear, step-by-step manner.
intro.usecase: Anagram checking is a fundamental pattern in text processing applications. You'll find it in search engines that suggest 'similar words' when you mistype a query, or in word games like Scrabble or Boggle where players need to find valid words from letter combinations. In developer tools, anagram algorithms help with code refactoring by identifying variables that are permutations of each other. This skill is essential for building features like intelligent search filters, content moderation systems that detect disguised inappropriate words, or educational apps that teach language patterns.

objectives: Implement a function that accepts two strings as input parameters
Construct logic to normalize input strings by converting to lowercase and removing non-alphabetic characters
Manipulate string data by splitting into arrays, sorting characters, and rejoining for comparison
Apply conditional logic to return true for valid anagrams and false for invalid ones
Initialize test cases to validate the anagram checker's behavior with different inputs
Integrate the anagram checker function into a simple interactive program
Configure the program to handle edge cases such as empty strings and different letter cases

steps.title: Create the main anagramChecker function
steps.instruction: Declare a function named anagramChecker that takes two parameters (str1 and str2) and returns a boolean.
steps.hint: You can use either a function declaration or arrow function syntax. The function should have two parameters and return true or false.
steps.expectedOutcome: A function named anagramChecker is created with two parameters and returns a boolean value.
successCriteria: The anagramChecker function is declared with two parameters (str1 and str2) and returns a boolean.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close! Make sure your function has exactly two parameters (str1 and str2) and returns a boolean value.
steps.feedbackWrong: The function isn't quite right. Check that you've named it 'anagramChecker', given it two parameters, and made it return a boolean.

steps.title: Normalize strings by removing spaces and converting to lowercase
steps.instruction: Inside your anagramChecker function, create two variables to store normalized versions of the input strings. For each string, remove all spaces and convert to lowercase.
steps.hint: Use the replace() method with a regex to remove spaces, then chain toLowerCase(). For example: str.replace(/\s/g, '').toLowerCase()
steps.expectedOutcome: Your function will have two variables containing the normalized strings, ready for comparison in later steps.
successCriteria: The function contains two variables that normalize the input strings by removing spaces and converting to lowercase.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you're normalizing both input strings (str1 and str2) and removing all spaces.
steps.feedbackWrong: create two variables inside the function that normalize str1 and str2 by removing spaces and converting to lowercase.

steps.title: Check if normalized strings have equal length
steps.instruction: Inside your anagramChecker function, add an early return check: if the lengths of the normalized strings differ, return false immediately.
steps.hint: Compare the lengths of the two normalized strings using the .length property. If they are not equal, return false.
steps.expectedOutcome: The function should return false early when the normalized strings have different lengths, preventing unnecessary further processing.
successCriteria: The function includes an early return check that compares the lengths of the normalized strings and returns false if they differ.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure to compare the lengths of the normalized strings and return false if they're different.
steps.feedbackWrong: The early return check is missing or incorrect. Remember to compare the lengths of the normalized strings and return false immediately if they differ.

steps.hint: Initialize an empty object (like const freq = {}), then use a for...of loop to iterate through the normalized string and increment counts in the object.
steps.expectedOutcome: The function will have an empty frequency object and a loop that counts characters from the first normalized string.
successCriteria: An empty object is initialized, and a loop iterates through the first normalized string to populate character counts.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track. Make sure you initialize an empty object and use a loop to count each character from the first string.
steps.feedbackWrong: Check the instructions: you need to create an empty object and loop through the first normalized string to count character frequencies.

steps.title: Return final result after verification
steps.instruction: After both loops complete successfully, return true from your anagramChecker function to indicate the strings are anagrams.
steps.hint: Add a return true statement at the end of your function, after all the verification logic.
steps.expectedOutcome: Your function should now return true when the strings are anagrams, after all previous verification steps pass.

steps.title: Create test cases to verify the function
steps.instruction: After your anagramChecker function, create several test cases with different string pairs and call the function with them. Log the results to the console.
steps.hint: Write console.log statements that call anagramChecker with different arguments, including both anagrams and non-anagrams.
steps.expectedOutcome: You should see console output showing true for anagram pairs and false for non-anagram pairs.
successCriteria: Test cases are created with different string pairs and anagramChecker is called with them, with results logged to console.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.

steps.hint: Call console.log with a descriptive message and the result from your anagramChecker function.
steps.expectedOutcome: After adding console.log statements, running the code will display the results of each test case in the console.

steps.title: Test edge cases (spaces, case sensitivity, special characters)
steps.instruction: Add three new test cases to your existing test suite: one with spaces, one with mixed case, and one with special characters.
steps.hint: Create test cases that verify your function correctly handles strings with spaces, different letter cases, and non-alphabetic characters.
steps.expectedOutcome: Your test suite will now include edge cases that verify the function handles spaces, case differences, and special characters correctly.

steps.hint: You can write a multi-line comment using /* */ or multiple single-line comments. Mention alternative approaches and their trade-offs.
steps.expectedOutcome: Your code will now include documentation about different optimization approaches for anagram checking.
successCriteria: A comment block discussing at least two optimization approaches (like sorting or using Map) is added to the end of the file.
